primitives.name: Fleet Task Classifier
primitives.verbatim_quote: Motif classifies your task (Fleet Router), routes to the best agent, QC's the output, and reports back.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'T': 'Task type (dimensionless categorical)', 'A_i': 'Agent i (indexed set of agents)', 'R(T, A_i)': 'Routing probability (unitless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Tasks are mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive; agent capabilities are static during routing.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When T ∉ dom(R), fallback to default agent.

layer2.mapping: Task classification function f(T) → argmax_i R(T, A_i) mirrors GSI's Bayesian update on task evidence.
layer2.telemetry: Routing accuracy rate over N tasks

primitives.name: Squad Leader Routing
primitives.verbatim_quote: Its "Squads with leader routing" maps 1:1 to your captains/players model.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'L_j': 'Leader j (captain)', 'P_{j,k}': 'Player k under leader j', 'C(L_j, P_{j,k})': 'Coordination cost (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Leadership hierarchy is stable; coordination costs are additive across players.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When C(L_j, P_{j,k}) > threshold, reassign squad.

layer2.mapping: Leader-player routing kernel K(L_j, P_{j,k}) = exp(-C(L_j, P_{j,k})) encodes squad efficiency in GSE's policy space.
layer2.telemetry: Average squad performance metric over time

reasoning_traces.think:
The fleet architecture embodies a layered control system where Motif serves as the primary orchestrator, applying task classification to route requests to specialized agents. This mirrors a Bayesian network where each agent represents a conditional probability distribution over outcomes. The squad leader routing mechanism introduces a hierarchical structure that enforces bounded rationality among subagents. Each leader-agent pair forms a micro-policy kernel, optimizing local coordination while maintaining global coherence. Failure modes arise when task classification fails (e.g., ambiguous input) or when leader-agent alignment breaks down due to misaligned incentives or communication bottlenecks. The command layer ensures top-down consistency but risks becoming a bottleneck under high concurrency.
